_meta.doc: Vibe Exchange dialogue pools (P2b). The foe's vibe is HIDDEN: 'openers*' must stay ambiguous — any line that telegraphs flirty/positive/negative breaks the gamble and belongs in 'reactions' instead. Flow: opener → player picks flirty/positive/negative/stoic → reactions[foeVibe][pick] reveals the vibe → outcome badge → battle. Line selection is seeded per (runSeed,row) — pools of 5+ keep repeats rare.

schema.openers: string[] — ambiguous pre-battle line, any regular trainer
schema.reactions: {foeVibe:{pick:string[]}} — the foe's vibe-revealing reply to your pick. Tone contract: flirty = charged innuendo / fade-to-black, never explicit; negative = raw toxic (temper, gaslight, humiliation, superiority — no slurs); positive = warm hype.
schema.reactionsT2: {foeVibe:{matchPick:string[]}} — deeper pools for the MATCH cell, unlocked at persona Tier 2. Escalates intensity.
schema.reactionsT3: {foeVibe:{matchPick:string[]}} — Tier 3 match pools. The ceiling: steamiest flirt / rawest toxic / warmest hype this file ships.
schema.postBattle: {foeVibe:{win|loss:string[]}} — foe's parting line on the victory (win) / defeat (loss) card. Rival is EXCLUDED here (getRivalAftermathLine already owns rival aftermath).
schema.repOpeners: {personaId:string[]} — 'word travels' openers that occasionally replace the ambiguous opener at persona Tier 2+. They speak about YOUR reputation and must not hint the foe's vibe.
schema.logBarks: {outcome:string[]} — one battle-log line at battle start, by exchange outcome.

_meta.editing: This file is the user-facing authoring surface. To push the flirty pools past the shipped ceiling (+18), replace or extend any 'flirty' arrays — the engine renders strings verbatim (HTML-escaped) and never inspects content. Keep lines ≤ ~110 chars so cards don't overflow.

openers: Mind the chalk. They only redrew it this morning.
You're the trainer they waved through at the last stop?
Let me put this bottle down. All right.
I heard Poké Balls in your bag before I saw you.
Keep your bag on your side. The wind keeps taking mine.
They left us enough room here for a match.
I've been trying to decide how to open this one.
I can wait if your team needs a moment.
We'll use your count, if you like.
My team is listening. So am I.
You want the near side or the far side?
Nothing to fill in here. Just give me a nod.
openersGymLeader: There's a scuff right where you're standing. Every challenger leaves one.
Wait for the door to latch. Then we can hear each other.
You can put your bag by the steps. Mine's there too.
They sent word you were ready. I'd rather hear it from you.
The ref will count us in. You tell me when.
I asked for a minute before the bell. This is it.
openersRival: I heard you coming past the last bend.
We always end up using the same side of the field.
I said I'd be ready before you got here.
Give me your first look. I want to remember it this time.
I've got something to say. You go first.
I kept the dry side for your bag.

flirty: Buy me a tea after this and I'll tell you which part of that worked.
We haven't even called our teams. Give me a chance to flirt back.
I like your nerve. I'm going to need it out there.
You're more fun to talk to up close. There, now you owe me a battle.
That's a good line. If we meet again, don't waste it on anybody else.
positive: I'll take good luck from you. I was going to ask for something less sensible.
You're nice to me. That's going to make this inconvenient.
I'll remember that next time the road's empty.
I could get used to people saying that where I can hear it.
Well, now I want to beat you politely. That's new.
negative: I was about to offer you the dry side. You can have the puddle.
I'd ask if you talked like that to everyone. I'd rather beat you and find out.
You had a much nicer expression before you opened your mouth.
I think I'll save the compliment for your Pokémon.
Fine. I'll put the kettle away.
stoic: All right. I'll do the introductions next time.
Not much for talking? I can think of worse ways to spend a match.
I had a joke ready. It probably needed a better audience.
Just the nod, then. I can read that.
Sorry, I mistook the stare for an invitation. First move?

flirty: Oh. I thought my face was warm from the walk.
That's kind of you. I've forgotten which pocket I put my lead in.
Give me a second. I didn't practice for that part.
I was doing fine until you said that. Where was I?
My teammate's looking at me now. See what you did?
positive: You too. Give my partner a chance to show you what we've been working on.
Thanks. We needed a good match today.
My partner heard that. See the ears?
I couldn't get that through to my team all morning. They heard it from you.
I'll take that with me. Ready?
negative: If that's your warm-up, my little brother wants it back.
My team can hear you. They just don't care.
Well, you're here. We can make a good battle out of that much.
That's all right. I used to say awful things when I got nervous too.
I'll wish your team luck separately.
stoic: A nod works. Good luck.
I'd rather get my timing right than my speech anyway.
My partner's more talkative than you. That's all we need.
Fine by me. Tell me with your first move.
I can wait one more breath if you're still choosing.

flirty: Do you try that on everybody? Don't answer. I won't like it either way.
Save it until you can stand on the other side of the field and say it.
I had a better answer in my head. We're battling now.
I don't need you looking at me like that while I'm trying to concentrate.
Go on. Smile all you like. I can still call a move.
positive: Save the encouragement until somebody asks for it.
Say that after you see what I brought.
You're spending a lot of breath on my side of the field.
Congratulate me if I win. Right now it sounds cheap.
You can be nice to the next person. I've heard enough today.
negative: Good. I was tired of being the only one willing to say it.
That's the first honest thing I've heard since breakfast.
Keep talking. I want to see when you run out of it.
Put that much behind the first move and we'll have a match.
Say it again after I take the lead.
stoic: That's fine. I have my own reasons to be angry.
Close your mouth all you want. I can see your hand.
Just stand there. You've got that part down.
I asked the last one if they were ready. Once was enough.
Look at your team, then. I don't need a thing from you.

flirty: I told myself I wouldn't ask you for a walk after. I've changed my mind.
Show me the move you don't let anyone else see coming.
Someone in town said you were good at this. I assumed they meant battling.
I'll remember the way you said that. You'll have to do better than that to win.

positive: I've had a rotten week. I needed to hear that from somebody who meant it.
My teammate wouldn't get up this morning. Look at the two of us now.
I keep forgetting I'm allowed to enjoy these. Thanks for the reminder.
I'll be glad I waited here however this goes.

negative: Good. I want you to mean every word when you're tired.
My old coach had a mouth like yours. Let's see whose habits I kept.
The road's been polite for days. I was starting to lose my temper.
Keep that edge. I hate being the only one left trying.

flirty: I'll be at the café after. We can finally finish a conversation without a bell.
I've been waiting to hear that since the last town. Now make me wait for the rematch.
Say it like that again when we're off the road.
I saved a seat where the window doesn't rattle. Come find me after the match.

positive: I've been practicing a first move just for you. My team knows how much this matters.
I walked back here yesterday in the rain. Hearing that, I'm glad I came back.
You get one battle like this in a whole season if you're lucky.
If I lose, I want it to be because you're better. That would be a good day too.

negative: They've all told me you're good. I want to hear you say it after I'm done.
Say what you really think when the first Ball goes quiet.
People keep ending these matches early. You'd better make me finish this one.
I've been chewing on this fight since they put your name up.

win: You won. Good thing I'd already planned on buying the tea.
That's a lot to ask of somebody who's trying to be charming. Nicely done.
Leave me the chalk so I can draw a line under that.
I owe you a rematch. You can have the good seat in the meantime.
loss: Have a seat until you feel better about losing. I'll keep you company.
I had to work much harder than I'm going to admit later.
Impressive. Next time I'm leaving my good coat at home so I can concentrate.
If you want another go, find me somewhere the wind isn't taking my hair.

win: That switch halfway through got me. Do you mind if we practice it?
My partner will be up for another match after a rest. So will I.
I'm glad you got to see how hard we tried.
I wish I'd brought somebody to watch that.
loss: You had me checking my bench. Ask for another round when you're ready.
My hands are still shaking. That's how close it felt from here.
Have some water. We can see where it went wrong when you've got your breath back.
My team got a lot from that. I hope yours did too.

win: Run it back another day. I want to see if you can do it twice.
Yes, I saw it land. Put your hand down.
Better read than mine. Don't make me say it twice.
I won't sleep till I figure out the switch you made.
loss: Heal your team first. You can think about it on the road.
Keep that opening if you like. I'll be ready for it again.
I expected a little more from the matchup.
You let me choose the pace. Don't do that for the next person.

flirty: They say you make friends on both sides of the chalk.
The woman with the ferry took a liking to you. She mentioned it twice.
I know you by description. They were thorough about what you said.
Someone at the last stop asked if you were coming back.
I've heard there can be quite a long conversation before you throw a Ball.
positive: A trainer at the next stop said you stayed until they felt up to walking.
Someone down the road was glad they'd asked you for a match. I thought I'd ask too.
My friend says you asked how her team was before you asked how she was.
They said you'd wish me luck if I told you this was my first time here.
The person you beat yesterday told me I ought to meet you.
negative: They said you'd have something to say before the first Ball.
The last trainer who fought you remembers your voice more than the match.
Your name came up at the counter. Nobody could agree on what you said.
Someone told me I should ignore the first thing out of your mouth.
I heard you had a way of shortening the conversation.
stoic: The keeper said to start when you nod.
Nobody could tell me what your voice sounds like.
I was told to leave out the speech. Fair enough.
Someone said you'd talk when your team needed to hear you.
People down the road seem to remember your moves more clearly than your face.
wildcard: I got two accounts of the same match. Both of them had you winning the first word.
They gave me three different reasons to wait here. You were in all of them.
I asked what to expect. The keeper said, 'From which one?'
Somebody described you all the way down to the shoes and still couldn't place you.
The stories I heard don't agree. I thought I'd see for myself.

buff: The exchange settles your nerves. Your team is ready to come out strong.
You got the better of the exchange. Your side starts with the edge.
The right words steady your side for the first call.
debuff: Your team felt that. The opening edge goes to the other side.
You misread the exchange. Your side starts a little unsettled.
Your call comes late. The exchange favored the other side.
neutral: Neither side takes an edge into the opening.
You square up. The exchange leaves things even.
The talk ends. Both teams start even.
